title: Context managers
summary: with statements, and writing your own.

steps.title: with
body: # the file is closed here, even if write raised

The object after `with` is a **context manager**. Its `__enter__` runs at the start (and its return value is bound by `as`); its `__exit__` runs at the end no matter how the block is left. Files, locks, database connections and temporary settings all use it.

steps.explain: `__enter__` runs on the way in, `__exit__` on the way out, so nested managers close in reverse order.

steps.title: __exit__ and exceptions
body: `__exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb)` receives the exception that ended the block, or three `None`s if it ended normally.
- Return `False` (or nothing): the exception carries on after cleanup.
- Return `True`: the exception is **swallowed**. Do this only deliberately, like a "suppress" helper.
return exc_type is not None and issubclass(exc_type, self.types)
The standard library already has this one: `contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError)`.

code: print("cleanup", exc_type.__name__ if exc_type else None)
steps.explain: Cleanup always runs. Returning `True` for `ValueError` swallows it; the `KeyError` gets `False` and continues to the outer `try`.

steps.title: @contextmanager
body: For most cases a generator is shorter than a class. Everything before `yield` is `__enter__`, everything after is `__exit__`:
yield name            # the value bound by `as`
print(f"</{name}>")   # runs even if the block raised
Put the cleanup in `finally`, or it will be skipped when the block raises.

steps.prompt: Arrange a generator-based context manager that prints `open` and `close` around the block.
In a `@contextmanager` generator, why wrap `yield` in `try`/`finally`?
options: So the cleanup still runs if the `with` block raises
So it can be used twice
steps.explain: An exception in the `with` block is re-raised at the `yield`. Without `finally`, the code after `yield` never runs.

steps.title: Indented printer
prompt: Write a context manager `indent()` (class-based or `@contextmanager`, your choice) and a function `say(text)`.
`say` prints `text` prefixed by two spaces for every `indent()` block it is inside. Nesting works, and the level must be restored even if the block raises.

level = 0
